exposure: lactation status (exclusive breastfeeding, mixed feeding, artificial feeding)
outcome: postpartum depression (measured by EPDS scores >=9 points)
cohort: The study included 809 nulliparous healthy women who had a vaginal singleton delivery at 37-41 weeks' gestation at a Japanese perinatal center between July 2018 and June 2019.
finding: The study found no significant association between lactation status (exclusive vs. mixed/artificial feeding) at one month postpartum and the development of postpartum depression.
